title: Triangle side across the x-axis
observableEvidence: Finds the length of a polygon side whose endpoints share an x-coordinate and lie on opposite sides of the x-axis, and labels it in units.
prompt: Triangle JKL has vertices J(-6, 4), K(-6, -7) and L(5, -7). What is the length of side JK? Include the unit in your answer.
solutionRepresentation: J and K have the same x-coordinate, so JK is vertical. J is 4 units above the x-axis and K is 7 units below it, so JK = 4 + 7 = 11 units. Equivalently, |4 - (-7)| = 11.
solutionMethod: Identify the shared coordinate, then add the distances from each endpoint to the axis (or take the absolute difference of the other coordinates), and label the length in units.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Whole-answer match after case, spacing and trailing-punctuation normalization; no substring parts. The linear unit is required: a bare number, or the number with a square or missing unit, is not accepted.

hintSteps.prompt: Compare the coordinates of J and K. When two points share one coordinate, the side between them is vertical or horizontal.
hintSteps.question: Which coordinate do J and K share?

hintSteps.prompt: Count the distance from J to the x-axis, then from the x-axis to K. A point below the x-axis is still a positive distance away from it.
hintSteps.question: How far is J above the x-axis, and how far is K below it?

hintSteps.prompt: On a different figure, the points (2, 3) and (2, -1) are 3 units above and 1 unit below the x-axis, so the side between them is 3 + 1 = 4 units long.
hintSteps.question: Using the same idea, how long is side JK, with its unit?

accessibilityNotes: Text-only item: all three vertices are given as signed coordinates in the prompt, so no plotted graph or color is needed. The answer is typed with its unit.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: Triangle JKL has vertices J at negative 6, 4; K at negative 6, negative 7; and L at 5, negative 7. Find the length of side JK and write the unit.
